title: 3 Papers on Antibody Tumor Penetration and Clearance
journal: Advanced Drug Delivery Reviews; Molecular Therapy; mAbs
one_line: A three-paper survey of how antibody format and size govern tumor penetration, tissue distribution, and clearance, spanning a classic review, a single-domain antibody-drug conjugate study, and a fragment biodistribution study.
key_claims: Thurber et al. (Adv Drug Deliv Rev) frame antibody tumor penetration as a competition between transport into tumor tissue and loss via systemic clearance plus antigen-mediated (binding-site barrier) clearance.
A highly stable human single-domain antibody-drug conjugate showed superior tumor penetration and treatment of solid tumors relative to conventional larger formats (Mol Ther).
Li et al. (mAbs) report that molecular size is a principal determinant of antibody fragment tissue distribution, with different fragment sizes giving distinct biodistribution profiles.
Together the papers support a size-versus-residence-time tradeoff: smaller formats penetrate tumors better but are cleared faster, while full-length IgG persists but distributes unevenly.
limitations: Show notes give no quantitative results, so specific penetration depths, clearance rates, or efficacy numbers are not recorded here.
The Thurber paper is a review/modeling piece rather than new experimental data.
Single-domain ADC results are from preclinical solid tumor models; clinical translation is not demonstrated.
Fragment biodistribution conclusions may be antigen- and model-specific and were not tested across all formats.
open_questions: Do head-to-head comparisons in the same tumor model show that improved penetration of small formats translates into better efficacy despite faster clearance?
Can half-life extension be added to small formats without reintroducing the penetration penalty of full-size IgG?
How much of observed distribution differences is size versus affinity and antigen-mediated clearance?
